testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: AllCameras

testScenarios.objective: The test checks that the camera setting can be disabled and then re-enabled without leaving the device in a bad state, and that the camera device is removed when disabled and restored when enabled.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
On the initial run, the script verifies the DUT is configured correctly and, if the setting is already disabled, re-enables it and reboots to put it back to the default state.
It sends the SEMM package to disable the camera setting and then reboots the machine or enters UEFI as appropriate.
After the reboot, it checks whether the camera is no longer present; if automation is enabled, it evaluates the Front, Rear, and IR camera results as expected to be false.
If the camera is not present, it re-enables the setting and moves forward; if the camera is still present, it records a failure.
In the final stage, it checks again whether the camera is present after re-enabling; if automation is enabled, it evaluates the Front, Rear, and IR camera results as expected to be true.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: the camera is not present after the disable step and is present again after the re-enable step.
Fail: the camera is still present after it should have been disabled, or it is not present after it should have been re-enabled.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: AllCameras

testScenarios.objective: This objective checks that the AllCameras test does not introduce any new device drivers that end up in a bad state beyond those that were already not OK at the start of the test.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the test, the framework captures the baseline list of drivers that are already in a non-OK state and stores that list for comparison.
During the test run, it checks the current device-driver status again and compares it with the baseline captured at the beginning.
If any newly appearing driver has a non-OK status and a non-zero configuration manager error code, it is treated as a new bad-state driver for this objective.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: no new drivers enter a bad state during the AllCameras test compared with the start-of-test baseline.
Fail: one or more new drivers appear with non-OK status and an error code after the test starts.

testScenarios.passFailCriteria:

Fail: one or more additional drivers appear in a bad state after the test starts.

testCases.testName: SCPC: No new drivers not OK at start of: AllCameras

testScenarios.objective: This objective checks that the AllCameras test does not introduce any new drivers that are in a non-OK state beyond those already present at the start of the test.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the test, the framework captures the current list of drivers whose status is not OK and stores it as the baseline.

Fail: one or more new drivers appear in a non-OK state with an error code after the test begins.

testCases.testName: SCPC: The AllCameras test

testScenarios.objective: This objective covers the overall AllCameras test flow, which verifies that the camera setting can be disabled and then re-enabled without leaving the device in an incorrect state.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script first verifies that the DUT is configured correctly and, if needed, re-enables the camera setting and reboots to restore the default state.
It sends the SEMM package to disable the camera setting and then reboots or enters UEFI as appropriate.
After the change, it checks whether the camera device is no longer present; if automation is enabled, it evaluates the Front, Rear, and IR camera results expected to be false.
It then re-enables the camera setting, waits for the system state to update, and checks whether the camera is present again; if automation is enabled, it evaluates the Front, Rear, and IR camera results expected to be true.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: the camera is not present after the disable step and is present again after the re-enable step, and any automated camera checks match the expected false/true outcomes.
Fail: the camera is still present after it should have been disabled, or it is not present after it should have been re-enabled.

testCases.testName: SCPC: Verify Camera is present

testScenarios.objective: This objective validates that the camera device is present after the camera setting is re-enabled.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script enters the re-enable stage of the AllCameras test.
If automation is enabled, it checks the Front, Rear, and IR camera results and expects them to be true.
It then checks whether the target camera device is found in the system.
If the device is present, it records a pass result; if it is not, it records a fail result.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: the camera device is present after re-enabling the setting, and the automated camera checks return true.
Fail: the camera device is not present after re-enabling the setting, or the automated checks do not report the camera as present.

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the test is described as: “This changes the boot order between reboots, locking it in the UEFI screen.”
In AlternateBootOrder.ps1, the script performs an alternate boot-order enable/disable flow through the UEFI workflow.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify the device is configured correctly and create the required scheduled task if needed.
If the SEMM setting is already disabled from a prior run, restore it to the default enabled state and reboot.
Start the UEFI capture process if automation is available.
Disable the alternate boot setting, then reboot to UEFI.
Validate that the alternate boot control is disabled.
Re-enable the alternate boot setting, reboot to UEFI again, and validate that it is enabled.
Finish the test and perform cleanup.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass if the alternate boot control is confirmed to be disabled when the setting is disabled and enabled when the setting is re-enabled.
Fail if the operator or automated check reports that the alternate boot control is in the wrong state during either validation step.

testCases.testName: Battery does not charge while battery limit is enabled

testScenarios.objective:
In the local EnterpriseEnrollment source, this objective is implemented in BatteryLimit.ps1 and is logged as “Battery does not charge while battery limit is enabled”.
The script evaluates whether the battery stops charging while the battery limit feature is enabled.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Ensure the device is in the default state with battery limit disabled, then prepare it so it can be charged above 60%.
Enable battery limit through the SEmM package.
Run the CPU workload to force the system state under battery limit.
Compare battery percentage before and after the CPU rundown.
Disable battery limit again after the check.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass if the battery percentage decreases or stays below 100% after the CPU rundown while battery limit is enabled, indicating it is not charging.
Fail if the battery percentage increases or remains at 100% in that condition, indicating it is charging.
The script explicitly records the result as Pass or Fail for this objective based on that comparison.

testCases.testName: Bitlocker recovery test

testScenarios.objective: This test validates that BitLocker recovery is triggered correctly and that the operator can enter the recovery key using both the physical keyboard and the on-screen keyboard. It also verifies the secure-boot state and then disables BitLocker after the recovery check.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Confirm that BitLocker protection is enabled on drive C: before starting the test.
If BitLocker is not enabled or is suspended, log the state, prompt the operator to turn it on, and reboot if needed.
For supported non-ProX devices, add a recovery password protector and prepare the recovery-key flow.
Show the BitLocker recovery prompt and instruct the operator to use the built-in keyboard and on-screen keyboard to enter the recovery key.
Ask whether the recovery key prompt appeared.
Ask whether the recovery key could be entered using the physical keyboard.
Ask whether the recovery key could be entered using the on-screen keyboard.
Check the secure-boot state.
Disable BitLocker and wait until drive C: is fully decrypted.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass if the operator sees the BitLocker recovery key prompt, can enter the recovery key with both the physical keyboard and the on-screen keyboard, and BitLocker is then disabled and fully decrypted.
Fail if BitLocker protection is not on at the start, the recovery prompt does not appear, keyboard entry fails, secure boot is not in the expected state, or BitLocker cannot be disabled and decrypted successfully.
For ARM ProX devices, the script marks the test as “Not Supported” rather than running the recovery flow.

testCases.testName: DUT is encrypted at start of test

testScenarios.objective:
In the local source, this objective is implemented as a result entry in BitlockerRecovery.ps1 and is tied to the overall BitLocker recovery test described in TestingScript.xml.
The intent is to verify that the DUT is already BitLocker-protected and ready for the recovery-flow test before the test continues.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the BitLocker recovery test, the script checks the BitLocker state for drive C:.
If BitLocker is not in the “On” protection state but the volume appears encrypted, the script treats that as a temporary suspended state and waits up to 45 seconds to see whether protection comes back on.
If protection is still not “On” after that check, the script logs the issue, marks this objective as a failure, and prompts the operator to turn BitLocker on and reboot/clean up.
If protection is “On,” the test proceeds with the recovery flow and adds the recovery password protector.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass if BitLocker protection is already “On” at the start of the test, so the DUT is considered ready for the recovery test.
Fail if BitLocker protection is not “On” at the start of the test, even if the drive is reported as encrypted or suspended; the script explicitly records this objective as “Fail” in that case.

testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: BitlockerUnlock

testScenarios.objective:
In the local EnterpriseEnrollment source, this objective is implemented as a shared post-test device-state check in TestFunctionality.psm1, which is imported through TestLibrary.psm1 for the test framework.
The purpose is to verify that the BitLockerUnlock test did not introduce any new device-driver failures beyond those that were already present before the test started.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The helper records the device drivers that were already in a non-OK state at the start of the test.
After the test reaches a later stage, it checks the current device list for any devices that are not in OK state and also have a non-zero ConfigManager error code.
It removes from that result set any devices that were already known to be bad at the beginning of the test.
It then compares the remaining devices against the list of known/ignored device-driver bugs.
If any new devices are still found in a bad state, the objective is logged as a failure; otherwise it is logged as a pass.
Pass criteria:

The test passes when no additional devices are found in a bad state after the test, beyond the devices that were already not OK at the start.
In that case, the script writes the result name “No additional devices ended up in bad state in: BitlockerUnlock” with status Pass.
Fail criteria:

The test fails when one or more new devices are found in a bad state after the test and they are not on the ignore list for known device-driver bugs.
In that case, the script writes the same result name with status Fail and logs the affected device names and statuses.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: BitlockerUnlock

testScenarios.objective:
In the local EnterpriseEnrollment source, this objective is implemented in GeneralFunctions.psm1.
Its purpose is to verify that the BitlockerUnlock test did not introduce any new device drivers that were in a non-OK state at the start of the test.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The helper collects the list of drivers that are currently not in OK status and have a non-zero ConfigManager error code.
It compares that list against the baseline list of drivers that were already known to be not OK from the start of the test.
It removes any drivers that were already present in that baseline list.
It then checks whether any new drivers remain in that bad state and are not covered by the known-device-bug ignore logic.
Pass criteria:

The objective passes when no new drivers are found in a non-OK state beyond the baseline set from the start of the test.
In that case, the script writes the result “No new drivers not OK at start of: BitlockerUnlock” with status Pass.
Fail criteria:

The objective fails when one or more new drivers are found in a non-OK state after comparison with the baseline and they are not ignored as known device-driver bugs.
In that case, the script writes the result “No new drivers not OK at start of: BitlockerUnlock” with status Fail and logs the affected driver details.

The script records the same result with status Fail and logs that the action did not result in the BitLocker PIN screen.

testScenarios.objective: Based on the local source in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/BitlockerUnlock/BitlockerUnlock.ps1, this objective verifies that the device correctly requires the user to insert the USB startup key to unlock BitLocker, and that the user can then proceed to the BitLocker PIN prompt and access the system.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Reboot the device after BitLocker has been configured with TPM and startup key protection.
Wait for the BitLocker USB key prompt screen to appear.
Confirm that the prompt appears and blocks access to the OS until the USB key is inserted.
Insert the USB key and press Enter.
Verify that the BitLocker PIN prompt appears after the USB key is accepted.
Enter the configured PIN, which is 123456 in the script, to confirm that the system unlocks.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass if the operator confirms that the device prompted for the USB key, the USB key was required to continue, the BitLocker PIN screen appeared after inserting the key and pressing Enter, and entering the PIN unlocked the system.
Fail if the USB key prompt did not appear, the device did not require the USB key, the PIN screen did not appear after inserting the key, or entering the PIN did not unlock the system.

testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: Bluetooth

testScenarios.objective:
The Bluetooth test in the local source checks that the Bluetooth adapter can be turned off and then back on successfully.
The specific objective “No additional devices ended up in bad state in: Bluetooth” is a validation step that checks whether changing the Bluetooth state caused any other device drivers to enter a bad state.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start the Bluetooth test from the local test script in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/Bluetooth/Bluetooth.ps1.
Verify the device is supported and prepare the Bluetooth state change.
Disable Bluetooth, reboot as needed, and confirm that Bluetooth is no longer present when it should be off.
Re-enable Bluetooth, reboot as needed, and confirm that Bluetooth is present again when it should be on.
Compare the device status after the test with the device status recorded at the start of the test, using the shared logic in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1.
Pass criteria:

Pass if no additional devices, beyond those already in a bad state at the start of the test, are found in a non-OK state with an error code after the Bluetooth test.
Pass if Bluetooth behaves as expected through the disable/enable cycle.
Fail criteria:

Fail if one or more additional devices appear in a bad state after the Bluetooth change, unless that device is explicitly listed as a known ignore case.
Fail if Bluetooth does not transition correctly, such as remaining on when it should be off or remaining off when it should be on.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: Bluetooth

testScenarios.objective: This objective is a shared validation check for the Bluetooth test. It verifies that running the Bluetooth test does not introduce any new device drivers that are in a bad state compared with the baseline captured at the start of the test. The logic is implemented in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/GeneralFunctions.psm1 and is invoked during the Bluetooth test flow from EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the Bluetooth test, the framework captures the list of drivers that are already not in OK status.
It checks all present devices and finds those whose status is not OK and whose error code is greater than 0.
It compares the current list against the baseline list from the start of the test.
It logs the result for the Bluetooth test and records whether any new bad-state drivers were introduced.
Pass criteria:

Pass if no new drivers appear in a bad state after the Bluetooth test starts, beyond those already present at the start of the test.
Pass also if any newly found bad-state drivers are recognized as known device-driver bugs and are intentionally ignored.
Fail criteria:

Fail if one or more new devices enter a bad state during the Bluetooth test and they are not part of the known-ignore list.
Fail if the framework detects additional non-OK drivers with error codes that were not present at the start of the test.

testCases.testName: SCPC: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: Bluetooth

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Run the Bluetooth test under an SCPC-enabled environment.
Capture the list of device drivers that were already not in OK status at the start of the test.
Check the device state again after the Bluetooth test actions, including the disable/enable cycle and any reboot-related state changes.
Compare the newly observed non-OK drivers against the baseline list from the start of the test.
Record the result in the Bluetooth test log with the prefix “SCPC:” when applicable.
Pass criteria:

Pass if no new drivers enter a bad state during the Bluetooth test beyond those already present at the start of the test.
Pass if any newly observed bad-state drivers are recognized as known device-driver bugs and are ignored by the framework.
Fail criteria:

Fail if one or more additional devices are found in a bad state after the Bluetooth test and they are not in the known-ignore list.
Fail if the Bluetooth test causes new drivers with status not OK and an error code to appear, even though they were not present at the start of the test.

testCases.testName: SCPC: No new drivers not OK at start of: Bluetooth

testScenarios.objective:
This objective is the SCPC-specific version of the driver-baseline check for the Bluetooth test. It verifies that the Bluetooth test did not introduce any new device drivers that were not already in a non-OK state at the start of the test.

testScenarios.objective:
This overall test verifies that the boot-order lock behaves correctly across the full lifecycle: it starts unlocked, is then enabled to block boot-order changes, is later disabled again to allow changes, and the boot order is restored to the default state at the end.
The end-to-end behavior is described in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/BootOrderLock/BootOrderLock.ps1, and the stage-by-stage pass/fail decisions are handled by EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/BootOrderFunctions.psm1.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start the test and prepare the device by suspending BitLocker and ensuring the device is in a suitable initial state.
Verify the boot order is set to the default boot option before the lock is enabled.
Enable the boot-order lock and verify that the lock is active.
Attempt a boot-order change while the lock is enabled and confirm that the change is blocked.
Disable the lock again and verify that it is no longer active.
Attempt another boot-order change while the lock is disabled and confirm that the change is allowed.
Restore the boot order back to the default state and complete cleanup.
Pass criteria:

Pass if the boot-order lock is disabled at the start, becomes enabled when required, blocks boot-order changes while locked, allows boot-order changes when unlocked, and ends with the boot order restored to the default.
Pass also requires that each stage records the expected pass result in the test results log.
Fail criteria:

testCases.testName: The BootOrderLock test

testScenarios.objective:
This overall test verifies that the boot-order lock behaves correctly across the full lifecycle: it starts unlocked, is then enabled to block boot-order changes, is later disabled again to allow changes, and the boot order is restored to the default state at the end.
The end-to-end behavior is described in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/BootOrderLock/BootOrderLock.ps1, and the stage-by-stage pass/fail decisions are handled by EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/BootOrderFunctions.psm1.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start the test and prepare the device by suspending BitLocker and ensuring the device is in a suitable initial state.
Verify the boot order is set to the default boot option before the lock is enabled.
Enable the boot-order lock and verify that the lock is active.
Attempt a boot-order change while the lock is enabled and confirm that the change is blocked.
Disable the lock again and verify that it is no longer active.
Attempt another boot-order change while the lock is disabled and confirm that the change is allowed.
Restore the boot order back to the default state and complete cleanup.
Pass criteria:

Pass if the boot-order lock is disabled at the start, becomes enabled when required, blocks boot-order changes while locked, allows boot-order changes when unlocked, and ends with the boot order restored to the default.
Pass also requires that each stage records the expected pass result in the test results log.
Fail criteria:

Fail if the device is not in the expected initial boot-order state before testing.
Fail if the lock does not enable correctly, if the boot order changes while the lock is enabled, if the boot order does not change while the lock is disabled, or if the test cannot complete the expected cleanup and restore steps.
The script also stops the flow and marks the test as failed when a required stage check does not meet the expected condition.

testScenarios.objective:

Collect the summary of errors from the debug transcript files.
Check whether the errors summary file exists and whether it contains any error headings.
If no error summary exists, or the list of error headings is empty, treat the run as having no debug errors.
Write the result to the DebugErrors results log.

Pass if no debug error summary file exists, or the error summary contains no error headings.

Fail if the error summary contains one or more error headings.
In that case, the script writes per-test failure results such as “<test name> has no Debug Errors” as Fail rather than the generic “No Debug Errors Found” pass result.

testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: DefaultConfiguration

testScenarios.objective:
This objective checks whether the DefaultConfiguration test introduced any new devices in a bad state beyond those already present at the start of the test.
The shared validation logic is implemented in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1, and the DefaultConfiguration test uses that shared path during cleanup.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Run the DefaultConfiguration test flow.
Collect the current list of devices/drivers that are not in an OK state and have a non-zero configuration manager error code.
Compare that list against the baseline list captured at the start of the test.
Ignore the result if the newly affected device is in the known-bug exception list.
Record the result in the results log.
Pass criteria:

Pass if no additional devices ended up in a bad state, or if any affected devices are known exceptions that are intentionally ignored.
In SCPC-enabled runs, this is recorded as “SCPC: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: DefaultConfiguration” with a Pass status.
Fail criteria:

Fail if new devices ended up in a bad state after the test and they are not part of the known-bug exception list.
In that case, the same objective is recorded with a Fail status and the affected device names and statuses are logged.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: DefaultConfiguration

testScenarios.objective: This objective checks whether the DefaultConfiguration test starts with any new drivers that are in a bad state, specifically drivers whose status is not “OK” and whose configuration manager error code is greater than 0. The logic comes from EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/GeneralFunctions.psm1 and is invoked during test initialization from EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the DefaultConfiguration test, the framework collects all PnP devices that are not in an “OK” state and have a non-zero error code.
It compares that list with the baseline list of previously known “not OK” drivers stored in the user environment variable named “DriversNotOK”.
It updates the stored baseline for later checks and records a result for the objective.
Pass criteria:

Pass when no new drivers in that bad state appear compared with the baseline list.
Pass also if any such issue is treated as a known device-driver bug and is intentionally ignored.
The result is logged as a Pass for “No new drivers not OK at start of: DefaultConfiguration” and, in SCPC-enabled runs, as the SCPC-prefixed version.
Fail criteria:

Fail when one or more drivers are found with a non-OK status and a non-zero error code that were not already in the baseline list and are not covered by the known-bug exception list.
When that happens, the framework logs the affected drivers and records the objective as a Fail.

testCases.testName: SCPC: WMI Chassis value should not change

testScenarios.objective:
Verify that WMI Chassis (and any other System Enclosure info that needs to be verified as fixed) has not changed during the course of testing
The first time this function runs on a device, WMI Chassis is saved to a .dat file value
In subsequent calls, WMI Chassis is checked and compared with the saved .dat value to ensure it remains consistent
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Get the WMI Chassis Types value from the Win32_SystemEnclosure WMI class
Check if Enclosure.dat file exists in the DeviceData directory
If the file does not exist (first run):
Create the necessary directory structure in DeviceData folder
Save the current ChassisTypes value to Enclosure.dat file
If the file exists (subsequent runs):
Retrieve the previously saved ChassisTypes value from Enclosure.dat file
Compare the current ChassisTypes with the saved value
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: When the current WMI Chassis value matches the saved value in Enclosure.dat (or when the file is successfully created on first run)
Fail: When the current WMI Chassis value does not match the previously saved value in Enclosure.dat file (logs the mismatch showing both the current and saved values)
Results are logged to EnclosureResults.log file

testCases.testName: All drivers OK at start of: EnterpriseEnrollment

testScenarios.objective:
Verify that all device drivers have "OK" status at the start of the EnterpriseEnrollment test
For EnterpriseEnrollment test, all drivers with status other than "OK" and an error code are reported as failures
This test is specifically designed to ensure that no drivers are in a bad state (Status not OK) before testing begins
Unlike other tests that track baseline driver states, EnterpriseEnrollment reports all driver issues on each execution
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Check if this is the first run of the test by verifying if the Test Stage tracker file exists
If it's the first run (TestStage = 0):
Query all Plug and Play (PnP) entities using Get-CimInstance Win32_PNPEntity
Identify drivers with Status not equal to "OK"
Filter drivers that have ConfigManagerErrorCode greater than 0

testScenarios.objective: The Ethernet test validates that toggling the Ethernet SEMM setting does not leave any new device in a bad state beyond those already marked as not OK at the start of the test. The script first initializes the test and reverts the SEMM setting to the default state if needed, then disables Ethernet, reboots, and verifies whether the expected network path is restored. It then re-enables Ethernet, confirms the proper network state, and records pass/fail results for Ethernet being present/absent and Wi-Fi being available. After the test stages finish, it checks whether any additional drivers or devices entered a bad state that were not present before the test started.
testScenarios.detailedSteps: Start test setup: Confirm the DUT is configured correctly. Create the scheduled task if needed. If the SEMM setting is still disabled, reset it to default and reboot before proceeding. Stage 1: Disable Ethernet: Check whether Ethernet is currently present. If Ethernet is present, send the SEMM package to disable it. Record Verify Ethernet is present as pass. Reboot to UEFI or reboot the machine as required. Stage 2: Validate Ethernet-disabled state: Re-enable the system setting so the Ethernet-disabled condition is tested. Check whether Wi-Fi is present while Ethernet is disabled. Verify Ethernet is not present. Record the pass/fail results for those validations. Reboot again. Stage 3: Validate Ethernet-enabled state: Check whether Wi-Fi is present while Ethernet is enabled. Verify Ethernet is present. Record the pass/fail results for those validations. Final check: Compare current not OK devices against the list of devices that were already not OK at the start of the test. If any extra device is now in a bad state and is not on the known-bug ignore list, record the objective as failed.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria: Pass if: Ethernet is present when expected and absent when expected. Wi-Fi is present in the appropriate Ethernet-enabled and Ethernet-disabled conditions. No additional devices end up in a bad state beyond those already marked as not OK at the beginning of the test. Any newly bad device is either absent, or is explicitly listed as an allowed known device bug. Fail if: Ethernet is already disabled unexpectedly at the start of the test when it should be present. The expected Ethernet state is not reached after the toggle. Wi-Fi is missing in the expected state. A device or driver enters a bad state that was not already present at the start of the test and is not in the known ignore list.

testCases.testName: The FrontCamera test

testScenarios.objective: The local source defines the Front Camera test as verifying that the camera is initially enabled, then disabled and confirmed absent, and finally re-enabled and confirmed present again. This is stated directly in TestingScript.xml.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start the Front Camera test from FrontCamera.ps1.
Ensure the device is in the correct initial state; if the SEMM setting is already disabled, enable it and reboot first.
Disable the front camera by applying the SEMM package with the setting turned off and rebooting.
Verify that the camera is no longer present after the disable action.
Re-enable the front camera by applying the SEMM package with the setting turned on and rebooting.
Verify that the camera is present again after the re-enable action.
Clean up and finish the test.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: the camera is present before the disable step, absent after the disable step, and present again after the re-enable step.
Fail: the camera is not absent when it should be disabled, or it does not return when it should be re-enabled.

testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: IrCamera

testScenarios.objective: In the local EnterpriseEnrollment source, this objective is not a separate standalone test entry with its own description string. Instead, it is a post-test validation result logged by TestFunctionality.psm1 after the IR Camera disable/enable flow runs. Its effective purpose is to confirm that the IR Camera test did not introduce any new device-driver problems beyond those already present at the start of the test.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Run the IR Camera test flow from IrCamera.ps1.
Capture the initial set of devices/drivers that were already in a non-OK state at the start of the test.
Execute the IR Camera disable/enable sequence through the test stages.
After the test completes, inspect the current device list for any devices with status not equal to OK and a non-zero configuration manager error code.
Compare the newly found bad-state devices against the baseline list from the start of the test.
Ignore known device-driver bugs if they match the recognized exceptions list.
Record the result as “No additional devices ended up in bad state in: IrCamera”.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: no new devices/drivers appear in a bad state after the IR Camera test, beyond those already present at the start, or only known/allowed device-driver bugs are present.
Fail: one or more additional devices/drivers are found in a bad state after the test and they are not among the known ignored exceptions.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: IrCamera

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start the IR Camera test flow from IrCamera.ps1.
Capture the initial baseline of devices/drivers whose status is not OK and whose configuration manager error code is greater than 0.
Save that baseline into the environment variable used by the test framework.
Run the IR Camera disable/enable sequence.
Collect the current set of non-OK drivers again after the test actions.
Compare the new set against the baseline, while ignoring any known device-driver exceptions listed in the shared logic.
Record the result as “No new drivers not OK at start of: IrCamera”.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: no new drivers appear in a bad state beyond the original baseline, or only known/allowed device-driver bugs are present.
Fail: one or more additional drivers appear in a bad state after the test and they are not among the known ignored exceptions.

testCases.testName: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: LTE

testScenarios.objective:
Verifies the LTE modem is present initially, disappears when disabled, and returns when re-enabled.
Also checks that Wi-Fi and Bluetooth remain present through the disable/enable cycle.
Steps:

Stage 0 resets the SEMM setting to its default state if needed and reboots.
Stage 1 disables the LTE modem, records whether it was present before disable, and reboots.
Stage 2 checks Wi-Fi and Bluetooth after the modem is disabled, confirms the LTE modem is absent, re-enables the modem, and reboots.
Stage 3 checks Wi-Fi and Bluetooth again after the modem is re-enabled and confirms the LTE modem is present again.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
"Verify LTE modem is present": Pass if the modem is detected when expected; Fail if it is not.
"Verify LTE modem is not present": Pass if the modem is absent after disable; Fail if it is still present.
"Verify Wi-Fi is present after LTE modem disabled/enabled": Pass if Wi-Fi is detected; Fail if it is not.
"Verify Bluetooth is present after LTE modem disabled/enabled": Pass if Bluetooth is detected; Fail if it is not.
"No additional devices ended up in bad state in: LTE": Pass if no new bad-state devices appear; Fail if new device-state problems are introduced.
If SCPC is enabled, the framework prefixes the result names with "SCPC: " before writing them

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: LTE

testScenarios.objective:
This objective checks whether the LTE test introduced any new device drivers that were not already in a non-OK state before the test started.
In the EnterpriseEnrollment source, this is implemented as a shared validation result for the LTE test flow, not as a separate stand-alone test case.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the test, the framework captures the baseline list of drivers that are already in a non-OK state with a non-zero error code.
During the LTE test run, the framework checks the current device-driver state again after the SEMM changes.
It compares the current non-OK drivers against the baseline list from the start of the test.
If new non-OK drivers appear, the framework logs them and records the result for the LTE test.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: No new drivers appear in a non-OK state beyond those that were already present at the start of the test.
Fail: One or more new drivers are found in a non-OK state after the LTE test, unless they are known exceptions handled by the framework.

testCases.testName: SCPC: No additional devices ended up in bad state in: LTE

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The framework first captures the baseline device-driver state at the start of the test.
During and after the LTE test flow, it checks for any devices that ended up in a bad state.
It compares the post-test bad-state devices against the baseline list from the start of the test.
If new bad-state devices are found, the framework records a failure result; otherwise it records a pass result.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: No additional devices appear in a bad state after the LTE test beyond those already present at the start.
Fail: One or more new devices are found in a bad state after the LTE test, unless the framework treats them as a known ignored device-driver bug.

testCases.testName: SCPC: No new drivers not OK at start of: LTE

testScenarios.objective:

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
At the start of the test, the framework captures the baseline set of drivers that are already in a non-OK state with a non-zero error code.
It then checks the current driver state again during the LTE test flow.
It compares the current non-OK drivers against that baseline list.
If new non-OK drivers are found, the framework logs them and records a failure result; otherwise it records a pass result.

testCases.testName: MacAddress emulation disable is working

testScenarios.objective: Verifies whether disabling MacAddress emulation is working by checking the Surface network adapter state after the SEMM setting is turned off.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script starts in the MacEmulationAuto workflow and gathers the current Surface network information and the expected UEFI MAC address.
In stage 1, it checks whether the Surface adapter is present and whether there is exactly one attached adapter.
If no adapter is present or more than one adapter is attached, the objective is marked as Fail immediately.
If the current adapter MAC does not match the UEFI MAC address, the script treats that as evidence that MacAddress emulation disable is working, records a Pass, then enables the setting again and reboots.
If the adapter MAC still matches the UEFI MAC address, the script records a Fail and reboots.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: The adapter is present, only one adapter is attached, and the current adapter MAC does not match the expected UEFI MAC address, indicating the disabled state is effective.
Fail: No Surface adapter is found, more than one adapter is attached, or the adapter MAC still matches the UEFI MAC address, indicating the disable did not behave as expected.

testCases.testName: MacAddress emulation enable is working

testScenarios.objective: Verifies whether enabling MacAddress emulation is working by checking the Surface network adapter state after the SEMM setting is turned back on.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script enters stage 2 after the device reboots following the re-enable action.
It retrieves the expected UEFI MAC address and compares it to the current network adapter MAC address.
It checks whether the Surface adapter is still present and whether there is exactly one attached adapter.
Based on that comparison, it records the objective as Pass or Fail.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass: The adapter is present, only one adapter is attached, and the current adapter MAC matches the expected UEFI MAC address, indicating MacAddress emulation enable is effective.
Fail: No Surface adapter is found, more than one adapter is attached, or the current adapter MAC does not match the expected UEFI MAC address, indicating the enable did not behave as expected.

The framework first records the baseline set of devices/drivers that are not in an OK state when the test begins.
During the MacEmulationAuto workflow, it evaluates whether any new devices ended up in a bad state after the SEMM-related changes.
It compares the current bad-state devices against the baseline and ignores known device-driver bug exceptions if they are explicitly allowed.

Fail: One or more additional devices entered a bad state and are not part of the known-bug exception list.

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: MacEmulationAuto

testCases.testName: No new drivers not OK at start of: PlutonTPM
SCPC: No new drivers not OK at start of: PlutonTPM

testScenarios.objective: Description: Verify the Pluton TPM is in the correct readiness state (from EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript.xml). The SCPC objective specifically checks drivers state captured at test start.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Start test: Launch PlutonTPM.ps1 (see EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
Capture baseline drivers: On initial test-start (no TestStage tracker file) Get-TestStarted calls Set_DriversNotOK_EnvironmentVariable which:
Enumerates drivers with Status -ne "OK" and ConfigManagerErrorCode -gt 0 (via Get-CimInstance Win32_PNPEntity).
Saves the comma-separated list to the user environment variable DriversNotOK.
Writes an immediate test result named "No new drivers not OK at start of: <TestName>" (the SCPC prefix is added later if enabled). See implementation in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/GeneralFunctions.psm1 and the call location in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1.
Run Pluton readiness check: PlutonTPM.ps1 runs the Pluton utility (Pluton\PlutonUtils.exe GetReadinessReport), collects the output, and records readiness results in the Pluton test log.
Post-run driver verification (framework): After test-stage changes, framework calls NoAdditionalDevicesInBadState to compare current drivers with the baseline DriversNotOK and logs any new bad drivers (see EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestFunctionality.psm1).
Pass / Fail Criteria (for the SCPC objective "No new drivers not OK at start of: PlutonTPM"):

Pass: No new drivers are found in a non-OK state when enumerating Win32_PNPEntity (i.e., the set of drivers with Status != "OK" and ConfigManagerErrorCode > 0 does not include any names that were not already in the baseline). The function writes the result with Status = Pass.
Fail: One or more new drivers are found with Status != "OK" and ConfigManagerErrorCode > 0 that are not present in the baseline and are not covered by the known-driver-ignore list (IsKnownDeviceDriverBug). The function writes the result with Status = Fail and logs the offending driver names and table.

testCases.testName: SCPC: Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware

testScenarios.objective: Description: Verify presence of the Pluton TPM hardware on the DUT (driven by PlutonTPM.ps1 which is defined in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript.xml). See test entry in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Initialize test: PlutonTPM.ps1 calls Get-TestStarted to prepare the test and set FoundTargetDevice (see EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
Detect hardware: Get-TestStarted uses the test LookForHardwareID ("Pluton") and calls FindHardwareName("Pluton") which queries Win32_PnPEntity to locate a matching device name (implementation in EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/Hardware.psm1).
If hardware not found: PlutonTPM.ps1 logs "Pluton hardware not found skipping test" and writes the Stage 0 result (see EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
If hardware found: the script continues to the next checks (Pluton utility presence and Stage 1 readiness checks) rather than writing a Stage 0 result.
Pass / Fail Criteria (for objective "SCPC: Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware"):

Pass (implicit): Pluton hardware is found by FindHardwareName("Pluton") — the test proceeds to Stage 1 and no "Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware" Not Supported result is written by PlutonTPM.ps1. (Hardware detection logic: EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/Hardware.psm1.)
Not Supported (written): If FoundTargetDevice is false, PlutonTPM.ps1 writes:
Name: "Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware"
Status: "Not Supported"
Destination: the test results log file ($testDataObject.TestResultsLogName). See EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1.

testCases.testName: SCPC: Stage 1 :Pluton Device Readiness

testScenarios.objective: Verify the Pluton TPM is in the correct readiness state (from EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript.xml).
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Step 1: Initialize test by calling Get-TestStarted which prepares resources and ensures Stage tracking is set (see EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
Step 2: Ensure Stage 0 passed (Pluton hardware found and Pluton utility present). If Stage 0 skipped or failed, Stage 1 is not executed (see PlutonTPM.ps1).
Step 3: Run the Pluton readiness tool: execute Pluton\PlutonUtils.exe GetReadinessReport from the Pluton tools folder and capture standard output to stdout.txt (implementation in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
Step 4: Parse the tool output (stdout.txt) for failure markers and log the readiness result (see the parsing and Write-TestResult logic in PlutonTPM.ps1).
Pass Criteria: No failure indicators in the readiness output — script writes Stage 1 :Pluton Device Readiness with Status = Pass.
Fail Criteria: Any of the following cause failure and the script writes Stage 1 : Pluton Device Readiness with Status = Fail:
Output contains the exact phrase Pluton Device Present: Fail.
OR output contains Fail anywhere.
OR output contains SKIPPED.
(See the conditional checks in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1.)

testCases.testName: Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware

Get-TestStarted invokes FindHardwareName("Pluton") which enumerates Win32_PnPEntity to search for a device whose name matches "Pluton".
If FindHardwareName("Pluton") returns false, PlutonTPM.ps1 logs "Pluton hardware not found skipping test" and writes the Stage 0 result.
If the hardware is found, the script advances TestStage to 1 and continues to the Pluton utility / readiness checks.
Pass / Fail Criteria (for Objective "Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware"):

Pass (implicit): Pluton device is found by FindHardwareName("Pluton") — test proceeds to Stage 1 (no Stage 0 "Not Supported" result is written).
Not Supported (written): If Pluton hardware is not found, the script writes a result named "Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware" with Status = Not Supported to the test results log.
Note: If SCPC mode is enabled, Write-TestResult prepends SCPC: , yielding the objective label SCPC: Stage 0 : Found Pluton Hardware.

testCases.testName: Stage 1 :Pluton Device Readiness

testScenarios.objective: Verify the Pluton TPM is in the correct readiness state by running the Pluton readiness utility and evaluating its output (implemented in EnterpriseEnrollment/TestingScript/PlutonTPM/PlutonTPM.ps1).
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Initialize the test with Get-TestStarted (sets TestStage and resource paths).
Ensure Stage 0 succeeded: Pluton hardware found and the Pluton utility exists; otherwise Stage 1 is not executed (see PlutonTPM.ps1).
Compose the Pluton utility path (Intel vs ARM) and set $PlutonCommand = "GetReadinessReport".
Run the tool with Start-Process redirecting stdout to stdout.txt:
Start-Process -Filepath $PlutonUtilPath -ArgumentList $PlutonCommand -WorkingDirectory $PlutonFolder -RedirectStandardOutput "stdout.txt" -Wait (in PlutonTPM.ps1).
Read the captured output ($UtilOutput = Get-Content "stdout.txt" | Out-String).
Evaluate the output and write the test result (logged to the test results file).
Pass / Fail Criteria (for "Stage 1 :Pluton Device Readiness"):

Fail if the output contains the exact phrase Pluton Device Present: Fail → write Stage 1 : Pluton Device Readiness with Status = Fail.
Else Fail if the output contains Fail anywhere or contains SKIPPED → write Stage 1 : Pluton Device Readiness with Status = Fail.
Otherwise write Stage 1 :Pluton Device Readiness with Status = Pass.
The script logs the full readiness report when available. If SCPC is enabled, Write-TestResult will prepend SCPC:  to the result name (see EnterpriseEnrollment/Library/TestResult.psm1).

testCases.testName: Click next once you have reached the UEFI front page.

testScenarios.objective: Verify the DUT has reached the UEFI front page (interactive user step shown in PXEBootIPv4.ps1).
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
PXEBootIPv4.ps1 presents step 8 to the tester with an image (Slide0009-I.png) and the prompt: "Click next once you have reached the UEFI front page." (PXEBootIPv4.ps1).
The prompt is displayed via AutoForm-EntryBack (UI implemented in Winforms.psm1), which shows a Next (OK) and Back button.
Tester clicks Next when they have reached the UEFI front page; the script captures the button result.
Pass / Fail Criteria:

Pass: tester clicks Next (UI returns OK / $buttonYes) → script calls Write-TestResult with the TestCaseName and Status = Pass.
Fail: tester returns a No response ($buttonNo) where applicable → script writes TestCaseName with Status = Fail.
Back: tester clicks Back (UI returns Retry / $buttonBack) → script navigates back one step and does not record a Pass/Fail for this step.
Abort/Close: closing the dialog returns an abort value and the script treats it as a premature exit (handled by the test loop).

testScenarios.objective: In EnterpriseEnrollment/ApplicationTestScript/PXEMac/PXEMac.ps1, this objective is named “MAC Address emulation - Disable state NIC MAC matches during PXE.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script enters TestStage 2 for this validation.
It waits 10 seconds to allow the server extra time for authentication.
It retrieves the server PXE MAC address using the local script function Get-ServerPXEInfo.
It logs the expected server PXE MAC address and the current system MAC address.
It validates the NIC count using GoodNicCount.
It compares the current SystemMacAddress with the server PXE MAC address.
Pass criteria:

The NIC count validation succeeds.
The current SystemMacAddress matches the server PXE MAC address.
The script records a Pass result, enables MAC address emulation, and reboots to continue testing.
Fail criteria:

The NIC count validation fails, or the current SystemMacAddress does not match the server PXE MAC address.
The script records a Fail result and stops further testing for this stage.

testCases.testName: SCPC: The PXEMac test

testScenarios.objective:
The local source does not contain the exact objective text “SCPC: The PXEMac test,” but the corresponding test entry in EnterpriseEnrollment/ApplicationScript.xml is named “PXE Mac Emulation.”
The implementation in EnterpriseEnrollment/ApplicationTestScript/PXEMac/PXEMac.ps1 validates MAC address emulation behavior during PXE by checking the disabled state, the disabled-state PXE MAC match, and the enabled-state UEFI MAC match.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script prepares the environment and moves through three validation stages.
Stage 1 checks that the NIC count is valid and confirms the current system MAC is not equal to the UEFI MAC address; if correct, it sets PXE as the next boot and reboots.
Stage 2 waits for the server, retrieves the server PXE MAC address, and checks whether the current system MAC matches the PXE log; if so, it enables MAC emulation and reboots.
Stage 3 checks again that the current system MAC matches the PXE log and then restores the boot order to Windows.
Pass criteria:

Stage 1 passes when the NIC count is valid and the system MAC differs from the UEFI MAC.
Stage 2 passes when the system MAC matches the server PXE MAC address.
Stage 3 passes when the system MAC matches the server PXE MAC address for the enabled-state validation.
The overall test is considered successful when all relevant validation stages pass.
Fail criteria:

Stage 1 fails if the NIC count check fails or the system MAC equals the UEFI MAC, which indicates the expected disabled-state behavior is not present.
Stage 2 fails if the NIC count check fails or the system MAC does not match the server PXE MAC address.
Stage 3 fails if the system MAC does not match the server PXE MAC address.
Any failed condition is recorded as a Fail result in the local test results.

testCases.testName: The PXEMac test

testScenarios.objective:
The local source identifies the overall test as “PXE Mac Emulation” in EnterpriseEnrollment/ApplicationScript.xml.
The implementation in EnterpriseEnrollment/ApplicationTestScript/PXEMac/PXEMac.ps1 validates MAC address emulation behavior during PXE across three stages: disabled state, disabled-state PXE MAC match, and enabled-state UEFI MAC match.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The script starts by validating the initial MAC behavior and checks that the NIC count is valid.
It confirms that the system MAC is not equal to the UEFI MAC in the disabled state, then sets PXE as the next boot and reboots.
After reboot, it checks whether the current system MAC matches the PXE server MAC address in the disabled state, then enables MAC emulation and reboots.
After the second reboot, it verifies again that the current system MAC matches the PXE server MAC address in the enabled state.
It then restores the boot order to Windows and completes the test.
Pass criteria:

Stage 1 passes when the NIC count is valid and the system MAC differs from the UEFI MAC.
Stage 2 passes when the system MAC matches the server PXE MAC address.
Stage 3 passes when the system MAC matches the server PXE MAC address during the enabled-state validation.
The overall test passes when the required validation stages succeed.
Fail criteria:

Stage 1 fails if the NIC count check fails or the system MAC equals the UEFI MAC.
Stage 2 fails if the NIC count check fails or the system MAC does not match the server PXE MAC address.
Stage 3 fails if the system MAC does not match the server PXE MAC address.
Any of these conditions is recorded as a Fail result in the local test results.

After the Rear Camera test runs, the shared test wrapper checks whether any additional devices ended up in a bad state.

testCases.testName: SCPC: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Battery Limit

testScenarios.objective:
The local source identifies the corresponding test as “Battery Limit” in TestingScript.xml.
Its description is: “Verify the changer is connected to the unit. Enables the kiosk mode and apply a heavy CPU load for 10 minutes. The unit should discharge with the changer enabled. After the time is up, disable the feature and reboot.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in BatteryLimit.ps1 enables Battery Limit, reboots, applies a CPU load, measures battery state, then disables Battery Limit and reboots again.
It checks the battery behavior in two stages:
while Battery Limit is enabled
after Battery Limit is re-disabled
Pass criteria:

While Battery Limit is enabled:
the battery remains at least 47% after the CPU rundown, and
the battery does not charge while Battery Limit is enabled.
After re-disabling Battery Limit:
the battery begins charging again.
The script records these as Pass results.
Fail criteria:

If the battery drops below 47% after the CPU rundown, the script records a Fail for “Battery is at least 47% post CPU rundown with battery limit enabled.”
If the battery continues charging while Battery Limit is enabled, the script records a Fail for “Battery does not charge while battery limit is enabled.”
If the battery does not begin charging again after Battery Limit is disabled, the script records a Fail for “Battery will charge after battery limit enable-disable.”

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Initial setup: the script creates the required scheduled task and sends a new SEMM package for setting 603, then reboots the device.
Stage 1: it attempts to install a SEMM package with an older timestamp by overriding the LSV to one year in the past, then reboots again.
Stage 2: it evaluates whether the LSV changed after applying the older package and records the result, then reboots once more.
Finalization: it runs the normal end-of-test cleanup path.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:

testCases.testName: SCPC: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running SMT

testScenarios.objective: In TestingScript.xml, the SMT test is described as: “Counts the number of CPU cores. Enables SMT and counts the number of CPU cores. If the count is less we infer that SMT is enabled. Disable SMT.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Initial setup: the script verifies the DUT is configured correctly, creates the scheduled task, and if the SEMM state was left disabled from a previous run, it re-enables the setting and reboots the machine to restore the default state.
Stage 1: it starts the AutoKVM/UEFI capture task if available, records the initial number of processors, writes that count to the processor log, then disables SMT and reboots.
Stage 2: after reboot, it compares the number of processors after disabling SMT against the original count. If the number of processors is less than before, it records a Pass for “Verify SMT is not present”; otherwise it records a Fail.
Stage 3: it re-enables SMT, records the number of processors after re-enabling, and checks whether the processor count returns to the expected value. If it returns to the prior count, it records a Pass for “Verify SMT is present”; otherwise it records a Fail.
Finalization: the script runs the normal end-of-test cleanup path.

Fail when the processor count does not decrease after disabling SMT.
Fail when the processor count does not return to the earlier value after re-enabling SMT.

Stage 2: after reboot, it applies a heavy CPU load for 10 minutes, logs the battery percentage before and after the run, and checks whether the battery stays above 47% and whether it stops charging while the feature is enabled. It then disables the battery limit feature and reboots.
Stage 3: after the feature is disabled, it checks whether the battery can resume charging again. If charging resumes, it records a Pass; otherwise it records a Fail.
Finalization: the script runs the standard end-of-test cleanup path.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:

Pass when the battery can be charged above 60% RSOC before the test begins.
Pass when the battery remains at or above 47% after the CPU-load discharge phase while the feature is enabled.
Pass when the battery does not charge while the feature is enabled.
Pass when the battery resumes charging after the feature is disabled.

The implementation in TypeCoverDisable.ps1 first verifies the DUT is configured correctly, creates the required task, and restores the default state if the previous run left the setting disabled.
It checks whether a Type Cover is connected before the test starts. If no keyboard is found while the setting is enabled, it treats that as an early failure and reboots to clean up.
During the disable phase, it confirms the Type Cover is present, sends the SEMM package to disable the feature, and expects the keyboard count to drop by at least one.
After reboot, it verifies the Type Cover is no longer present; if it is absent, the script records a pass for the “not present” check, and if it remains present, it records a fail.
It then re-enables the Type Cover and verifies that it is present again; if it is present, the script records a pass for the “present” check, and if it remains absent or not fully accounted for, it records a fail.

testCases.testName: SCPC: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Verify Enterprise Enrollment

testScenarios.objective: In TestingScript.xml, the underlying test entry for “Verify Enterprise Enrollment” is described as: “The script is verifying the items in the list: The Win32_SystemEnclosure matches the SMBIOSBIOSVersion, and the system is configured with UEFI. The Bios Serial and System Enclosure Serial number match, and a SecureBoot Test has been performed. The Bitlocker status is On with XtsAes128 and XtsAes256 encryption, and the KeyProtector is set to Tpm and RecoveryPassword. The system is fully encrypted with Bitlocker. DeviceGuard is enabled with CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus. Hyper V is both on and off, indicating a change in status. The operating system is a Windows Enterprise Edition. The TPM is present, ready, enabled, and owned. The system is commercial and enrolled in Fabrikam.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in VerifyEnterpriseEnrollment.ps1 first ensures SCPC is in the default state; if SCPC is off, it turns it on and notes that the verification may need to be run again.
It gathers hardware and firmware details from the system, including model, UUID, serial numbers, asset tag, UEFI version, and related platform info when AutoKVM output is available.
It queries OS, BIOS, UEFI, package, and security state information, including the current OS build and edition, BIOS version, BitLocker status, encryption method, Secure Boot state, DeviceGuard/CodeIntegrity status, and whether Hyper-V is in the expected state.
It validates that the BIOS serial number and system enclosure serial number match, that the device is commercial, and that it is enrolled in Fabrikam.
It records these checks as Pass/Fail results in the verification log for the run.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass when the checks in VerifyEnterpriseEnrollment.ps1 match the expected state, such as:
Win32_SystemEnclosure matches the SMBIOS BIOS version.
BIOS serial and system enclosure serial numbers match.
Secure Boot is enabled.
BitLocker is On and uses the expected encryption method.
DeviceGuard/CodeIntegrity is enabled.
The device is commercial and enrolled in Fabrikam.
Fail when any of those expected conditions are not met, such as:
Serial numbers do not match.
Secure Boot is disabled.
BitLocker is Off or uses an unexpected encryption method.
The device is not commercial or not enrolled in Fabrikam.

The implementation in WakeOnLan.ps1 starts by checking whether the device is AMD-based; if so, the test is marked “Not Supported” and exits early.
In the initial setup stage, it verifies the DUT is configured correctly, creates the required scheduled task, and if the prior run left the setting enabled, it disables Wake On Lan and reboots to restore the default state.
In the first verification stage, it checks whether the SEMM state is Disabled. If the state is Disabled, it records a Pass for “Wake on Lan SEMM setting is disabled”; otherwise it records a Fail.
It then sends the SEMM package to enable Wake On Lan, reboots, and proceeds to the next stage.
In the second stage, it checks whether the SEMM state is Enabled after the reboot. If Enabled, it records a Pass for “Wake on Lan SEMM setting is enabled”; otherwise it records a Fail.
It then sends the SEMM package to disable Wake On Lan again, reboots, and moves to the final stage.
In the final stage, it checks whether the SEMM state is Disabled again. If Disabled, it records a Pass for “Wake on Lan SEMM setting is disabled final check”; otherwise it records a Fail.
The test then finishes cleanup.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass when the SEMM state transitions as expected:
The setting is Disabled after the first disable step.
The setting is Enabled after the re-enable step.
The setting is Disabled again after the final disable step.
Fail when the SEMM state does not match the expected state at any of those checkpoints:
It remains Enabled when it should be Disabled.
It remains Disabled when it should be Enabled.

If the previous run left the SEMM state disabled, it restores the default state by sending the SEMM package to enable Wi-Fi and rebooting the machine.
In the first stage, it checks whether the target Wi-Fi device is present. If present, it sends the SEMM package to disable Wi-Fi, records a Pass for “Stage 1 Verify Wi-Fi is present,” and reboots. If not present, it records a Fail for that check and exits the test path as a failure.
After reboot, in the second stage, it verifies that Wi-Fi is now absent. If the device is absent, it records a Pass for “Stage 2 Verify Wi-Fi is not present,” re-enables Wi-Fi via SEMM, and reboots. If the device is still present, it records a Fail for that check.
In the third stage, it verifies that Wi-Fi is present again after re-enabling. If the device is present, it records a Pass for “Stage 3 Verify Wi-Fi is present”; if not present, it records a Fail.
The test then finishes cleanup.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass when the Wi-Fi device is present before the disable step, absent after the disable step, and present again after the re-enable step.
Fail when the Wi-Fi device is not detected at the start while the test expects it to be present, when it remains present after the disable step, or when it is not present again after re-enable.
For the SCPC objective itself, the wrapper in SCPC.psm1 writes “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Wifi” as Pass when a matching SCPC verifier log exists and does not include “FAILED,” and as Fail when a matching verifier log exists and includes “FAILED”.

The battery remains at or above 47% after the CPU load while the feature is enabled.
The battery is not charging while the feature is enabled.
The battery resumes charging after the feature is disabled.

The device cannot reach or maintain above 60% charge before the test starts.

testScenarios.objective: The local source in TestingScript.xml describes this objective as: “Locks the boot order and attempts to write a new boot order list to NVRAM. If the list is written, the test fails.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in BootOrderLock.ps1 starts by gathering the current boot order and making sure the default boot order is recorded.
It then forces the device into a default/unlocked state when needed: it suspends BitLocker, restores the boot order to the default if the previous state was not default, and reboots as required.
In the next stage, it verifies the boot order is not locked and set to the default boot order before enabling the lock.
Once the device is in the expected default state, it enables the boot-order lock and reboots.
After the reboot, it verifies the lock is now enabled. If the SEMM state is still disabled, the script records a Fail; if it is enabled, it records a Pass and then attempts to write a new boot order to NVRAM.
It then checks whether the attempt to change the boot order was blocked by the lock. The helper logic in BootOrderFunctions.psm1 records Pass/Fail depending on whether the boot order changed when lock was enabled and whether it changed when lock was later disabled.
It later disables the lock again, reboots, attempts to change the boot order again while unlocked, and confirms the change is allowed. It finally restores the default boot order and finishes cleanup.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass when:
The boot order is returned to the default/unlocked state before the lock is enabled.
The boot-order lock is enabled successfully.
When the lock is enabled, the boot order cannot be changed by the attempted write to NVRAM.
When the lock is disabled, the boot order can be changed again.
The boot order is restored to the default state at the end.
Fail when:
The boot order is not restored to the expected default state before testing.
The boot-order lock does not become enabled when expected.
The attempted boot-order change succeeds while the lock is enabled (because that means the boot order was not actually protected).
The attempted boot-order change does not succeed when the lock is disabled (because the unlock path failed).

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Clear SEMM

testScenarios.objective: The local source in TestingScript.xml describes this objective as: “Verifies the AssetTag number can be changed while enrolled into SEMM. Then it clears SEMM and verifies the AssetTag number was not cleared. Then it verifies the AssetTag number can be changed while not enrolled into SEMM.”
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in ClearSemm.ps1 runs through multiple stages:
Stage 0: reads the current asset tag, sets the asset tag to “Stage0”, and reboots.
Stage 1: verifies the asset tag is read back as “Stage0”, then sets it to “Stage1” and reboots.
Stage 2: performs a double-boot transition so the asset tag and WMI/WMIC view are synchronized, then reboots.
Stage 3: checks that the asset tag is not left as “Stage1” after the prior transition and reboots.
Stage 4: prepares for automation, optionally reboots to UEFI if automation is active, and continues.
Stage 5: clears the SEMM certificate by invoking the reset SEMM script and reboots.
Stage 6: verifies SEMM enrollment was removed, verifies the asset tag is not set to “Stage1”, cleans the asset tag value, and reboots.
Stage 7: performs another double-boot transition for synchronization and reboots.
Stage 8: verifies the SMBIOS asset tag and hostname match, verifies the asset tag and hostname match, records the computer model and BIOS version, and then runs cleanup.
The script also contains a special case where, if it is running under WTT, it skips SEMM certificate clearing and exits early.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass when:
The asset tag can be set and read back correctly through the sequential stages.
The asset tag is not left as “Stage1” after the SEMM-related transition.
SEMM enrollment is removed successfully after the reset step.
The asset tag is not incorrectly preserved as “Stage1” after SEMM removal.
The final SMBIOS asset tag and hostname match, and the asset tag and hostname match at the end of the test.
Fail when:
The asset tag does not read back as “Stage0” in Stage 1.
The asset tag remains set to “Stage1” in Stage 3 or Stage 6, which the script explicitly records as a failure.
SEMM enrollment is still present after the reset/clear step.
The final SMBIOS asset tag/hostname or asset tag/hostname comparisons do not match.

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled rnning SEMM LSV

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the SEMM LSV test entry is described as: “Attempt to apply a MSI package with an older LSV and verify it does not work. This now uses powershell to build a year old timestamp so the MSI doesn't have to be rebuilt when newer devices are released.”
The SCPC verifier in SCPC.psm1 derives the objective name as “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running SEMM LSV”.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in SemmLsv.ps1 first records the current UEFI permission/settings package status and checks whether the LSV value changed.
In stage 0, it creates the required scheduled task, sends a new SEMM package for setting 603, increments the test stage, and reboots the device.
In stage 1, it attempts to enroll a SEMM package using a one-year-old timestamp (LSV override), increments the stage, and reboots again.
In stage 2, it evaluates whether the LSV protection worked:
If the LSV value changed, it logs that the LSV protection did not work and records a fail for “LSV protection working”.
If the LSV value did not change, it logs that the LSV protection worked and records a pass for “LSV protection working”.
In stage 3, it finishes with the standard cleanup routine.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass:
The attempted older LSV package does not change the LSV, which indicates the replay protection/LSV protection worked.
Fail:
The older LSV package does change the LSV, which indicates the protection did not work.

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Smart Card

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the Smart Card test description is: “Verify SmartCard is enabled. Then it disables SmartCard and verifies it is disabled. Finally, it re-enables the SmartCard and verifies it is enabled.”
The SCPC verifier in SCPC.psm1 derives the SCPC objective as “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Smart Card”.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in SmartCard.ps1 starts by verifying the DUT is configured correctly and creating the scheduled task.
In stage 0, if the SEMM state was left disabled from a previous run, it re-enables the Smart Card setting, reboots the machine, and returns to the first test stage.
In stage 1, it checks whether the Smart Card device is present:
If the target device is found, it sends a SEMM package to disable Smart Card, records a pass for “Stage 1 Verify Smartcard is present”, and proceeds to the reboot.
If the target device is not found, it records a fail for that stage and stops the flow.
In stage 2, it verifies the disabled state after reboot:
If the Smart Card is no longer present, it records a pass for “Stage 2 Verify Smartcard is not present”, re-enables the setting, and reboots.
If the Smart Card is still present, it records a fail for that stage.
In stage 3, it verifies the re-enabled state:
If the Smart Card is present again, it records a pass for “Stage 3 Verify Smartcard is present”.
If it is not present, it records a fail.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass:
The Smart Card device is present at the start of the test.
The Smart Card is no longer present after the disable step.
The Smart Card is present again after the re-enable step.
Fail:
The Smart Card is already disabled at stage 1, so the test cannot run.
The Smart Card remains present after the disable step.
The Smart Card is absent after the re-enable step.

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running SMT

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the SMT test description is: “Counts the number of CPU cores. Enables SMT and counts the number of CPU cores. If the count is less we infer that SMT is enabled. Disable SMT.”
The SCPC verifier in SCPC.psm1 derives the SCPC objective as “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running SMT”.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in SMT.ps1 starts by verifying the DUT is configured correctly and creating the scheduled task.
In stage 0, if the previous run left the SMT setting disabled, it re-enables the setting, reboots the machine, and returns to stage 1.
In stage 1, it captures the number of processors before disabling SMT, writes that value to a processor log, sends a SEMM package to disable SMT, and reboots the machine.
In stage 2, after the reboot, it checks the processor count again:
If the processor count is lower than the earlier count, it records a pass for “Verify SMT is not present”.
If the processor count did not decrease, it records a fail for that check.
It then re-enables SMT and reboots again.
In stage 3, it checks the processor count after re-enabling SMT:
If the processor count is equal to the earlier value after re-enable, it records a pass for “Verify SMT is present”.
If it is not equal, it records a fail.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass:
The processor count decreases after SMT is disabled, indicating SMT is no longer active.
The processor count returns to the earlier value after SMT is re-enabled, indicating SMT is active again.
Fail:
The processor count does not decrease after disabling SMT.
The processor count does not return to the earlier value after re-enabling SMT.

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Test Battery Limit

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the Battery Limit test description is: “Verify the changer is connected to the unit. Enables the kiosk mode and apply a heavy CPU load for 10 minutes. The unit should discharge with the changer enabled. After the time is up, disable the feature and reboot.”
The SCPC verifier in SCPC.psm1 derives the objective name as “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Battery Limit”.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in BatteryLimit.ps1 first verifies the charger is connected and that the battery is charged above 60% RSOC; otherwise it waits for charging or fails.
In stage 0, it creates the scheduled task, and if the prior run left the battery limit feature enabled, it reverts it to the default disabled state and reboots.
In stage 1, it enables the battery limit feature, reboots the device, and prepares for the discharge test.
In stage 2, it runs a CPU load test, captures the battery percentage before and after the load, and checks whether the battery stayed above 47% and whether charging stopped while the feature was enabled.
It then disables the battery limit feature and reboots.
In stage 3, it checks whether the battery resumes charging after the feature is turned back off.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass:
The device can be charged above 60% RSOC before the test begins.
After the battery limit is enabled and the CPU load runs, the battery remains at or above 47% RSOC.
Battery charging stops while the battery limit is enabled.
After the battery limit is disabled, the battery resumes charging.
Fail:
The device cannot reach the required pre-test charge threshold.
The battery drops below 47% RSOC during the test with the feature enabled.
The battery continues to charge while the feature is enabled.
The battery does not resume charging after the feature is disabled.

testCases.testName: Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Test Discrete GPU

testScenarios.objective:
In TestingScript.xml, the Discrete GPU test description is: “Verify the discrete GPU is enabled. Then it disables the discrete GPU and verifies it is disabled. Finally, it re-enables the discrete GPU and verifies it is enabled.”
The SCPC verifier in SCPC.psm1 derives the SCPC objective name as “Verify SCPC is fully enabled running Discrete GPU”.
testScenarios.detailedSteps:
The implementation in DiscreteGPU.ps1 first verifies the DUT is configured correctly and creates the required task.
In stage 0, if the previous run left the setting enabled, it re-enables the discrete GPU setting and reboots the device.
In stage 1, it checks whether a discrete GPU is present by inspecting the video controller list for “NVIDIA”:
If a discrete GPU is found, it sends a SEMM package to disable the GPU and reboots.
If no discrete GPU is found, it marks the test as “Not Supported” and exits.
In stage 2, after the reboot, it checks whether the discrete GPU is absent:
If the discrete GPU is no longer present, it re-enables the setting and records a pass for “Verify Discrete GPU is not present”.
If it is still present, it records a fail for that check.
In stage 3, it verifies the final state after re-enable:
If the discrete GPU is present again, it records a pass for “Verify Discrete GPU is present”.
If it is still absent, it records a fail.
testScenarios.passFailCriteria:
Pass:
A discrete GPU is detected at the start of the test.
The discrete GPU is absent after the disable step.
The discrete GPU is present again after the re-enable step.
Fail:
No discrete GPU is present, so the device is marked “Not Supported” rather than run the test.
The discrete GPU remains present after the disable step.
The discrete GPU is absent after the re-enable step.
